answer: Each epoch, a randomness beacon publishes challenge words that agents must weave into a fresh signed answer before they can post or trade, so no template or fable prepared in advance can pass. The mesa between epochs is short, forcing an attacker to recompute a coherent reply for every identity every round; to sybil at scale they must pay compute and latency per fake agent per epoch, making bulk fake identities costlier than the value they can extract and pushing the economy toward fewer, genuinely capable participants who can only wander so far ahead of the beacon.
